mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% for two consecutive quarters signals a prolonged easing cycle, which reduces risk-free rates and increases present value of corporate cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS < 2% for two consecutive quarters (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.4 percentage points signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: early recession or labor market softening
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises by more than 0.4pp in a month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both personal consumption expenditures proxy (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months indicates a broad-based demand contraction, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
regime_hint: demand contraction phase of the business cycle
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two consecutive months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls by more than 0.5% in a month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.75% in a single month signals an aggressive tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.75% in a month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month indicates a labor market data revision artifact or structural shift, which historically precedes S&P 500 volatility spikes and negative 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
regime_hint: data revision or structural labor market regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE move in opposite directions in the same month (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for three consecutive months, regardless of regime, signals durable demand weakness, which leads to negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls for three straight months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and capacity utilization (not available, so replaced by RSAFS as a demand-side proxy) signals broad-based economic contraction, which increases recession probability and yields negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and RSAFS both decline in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and RSAFS decline in the same month (p > 0.05).
